issues.legal_issue: Immovable property sold for full consideration and handed over to purchasers without a registered conveyance remains part of the transferor’s net wealth when legal title remains with the transferor.
material_facts: The transferor had received the full sale consideration and handed possession of the properties to the purchasers.
No registered sale deeds had been executed, so legal title remained with the transferor.
The purchasers could retain possession against the transferor and could seek a conveyance, but the transferor retained title enforceable against others.
issues.conclusion: The properties belonged to the transferor for the purpose of calculating net wealth and were includible in the transferor’s net wealth.
issues.legal_principle: Sections 3 and 2(m) of the Wealth-tax Act, 1957 make wealth tax chargeable on net wealth, including assets belonging to the assessee. “Belonging to” is not limited to absolute ownership, but legal title is material. Mere possession does not make an asset belong to its possessor. Section 53A of the Transfer of Property Act, 1882 protects possession as a shield; it does not transfer legal title. The Court relied on Commissioner of Wealth-tax, West Bengal v. Bishwanath Chatterjee and Raja Mohammad Amir Ahmed Khan v. Municipal Board of Sitapur, and approved Commissioner of Wealth-tax, Gujarat-IV v. H.H. Maharaja F.P. Gaekwad.

rule.if: wealth_tax_assessment and full_sale_consideration_paid and possession_transferred_to_purchaser and no_registered_conveyance and legal_title_retained_by_transferor

predicates.wealth_tax_assessment: The proceeding determines whether property is included in a person’s net wealth for wealth-tax purposes.
predicates.full_sale_consideration_paid: The purchaser paid the transferor the full agreed consideration for the property.
predicates.possession_transferred_to_purchaser: The transferor handed possession of the property to the purchaser.
predicates.no_registered_conveyance: The parties did not execute a registered conveyance transferring legal title to the purchaser.
predicates.legal_title_retained_by_transferor: The transferor retained legal title to the property despite the sale arrangement and transfer of possession.

issues.definition: When a wealth-tax assessment concerns property for which the full price has been paid and possession transferred but no registered conveyance has passed legal title, the property is included in the transferor’s net wealth if the transferor retained legal title.

issues.legal_issue: A fixed annual payment made in lieu of prior income is exempt from inclusion in net wealth when the arrangement precludes its commutation into a lump sum.
material_facts: The payment was a fixed annual sum made in lieu of the recipient’s previous income from an estate taken over by the government.
The payment formed part of an arrangement that also provided separate annual sums for a personal allowance and the upkeep of palaces.
The recipient had no right under the arrangement to demand that the annual payment be commuted into a lump sum.
The related personal allowance was not commutable, and the Court found that commutation of the payment would defeat the arrangement’s purpose.
issues.conclusion: The annual payment was an annuity, but the arrangement precluded its commutation into a lump sum; the right to receive it was therefore exempt from inclusion in net wealth.
issues.legal_principle: Section 2(e)(iv) of the Wealth-tax Act, 1957 excludes a right to an annuity where its terms and conditions preclude commutation of any portion into a lump sum. An annuity is a fixed sum of money payable annually. Whether commutation is precluded may be inferred from the payment arrangement and its circumstances, even without an express clause. The Court relied on Ahmed G.H. Ariff v. Commissioner of Wealth-tax, Arundhati Balkrishna, Commissioner of Wealth-tax v. Her Highness Maharani Gayatri Devi of Jaipur, Commissioner of Wealth-tax v. P.K. Banerjee, and H.H. Maharajadhiraja Madhav Rao Jiwaji Rao Scindia Bahadur v. Union of India.

rule.if: wealth_tax_assessment and fixed_annual_payment and payment_in_lieu_of_prior_income and integrated_payment_arrangement and recipient_has_no_right_to_commute_payment and arrangement_context_precludes_commutation

predicates.wealth_tax_assessment: The proceeding determines whether a right to receive a payment is included in a person’s net wealth for wealth-tax purposes.
predicates.fixed_annual_payment: The payer undertook to pay the recipient a fixed sum each year.
predicates.payment_in_lieu_of_prior_income: The payer made the annual payment in place of income the recipient had previously received from property taken over by the payer.
predicates.integrated_payment_arrangement: The annual payment formed part of a broader arrangement that provided other payments for distinct purposes.
predicates.recipient_has_no_right_to_commute_paymen: The arrangement gave the recipient no right to demand conversion of the annual payment into a lump sum.
predicates.arrangement_context_precludes_commutatio: The circumstances and purpose of the arrangement showed that converting the payment into a lump sum would defeat that arrangement.

issues.definition: When a wealth-tax assessment concerns a fixed annual payment made in lieu of prior income, the right to receive it is excluded from assets if the recipient has no right to commute it and the arrangement’s context precludes commutation.
